subject: Trial top-up request — procurement hold at Healthlytics
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@healthlytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Healthlytics Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot wrap-up: procurement delay and request for short-term top-up

Hi Vanessa,

Quick note — we're in the final stretch of the Redwood pilot and the team is ready to run the last benchmark set, but our procurement/Legal team has put the PO on hold pending an updated security addendum. That review is expected to finish next week, but it means the pilot access and the credit allotment tied to the trial will lapse on Feb 22.

Would Redwood be able to provision a short-term trial top-up (either credit or a 2-week access extension) so we can complete the evaluation? We're aiming to validate production throughput and a few latency scenarios; we estimate ~8k–12k extra inference tokens needed. If you need specifics, I've attached the benchmark-plan.xlsx with the test matrix.

Procurement is aware and has opened an expedited ticket, but I wanted to check with you directly so we don't lose the momentum.

Thanks — appreciate any flexibility here.

Elena Park
Lead ML Engineer, Healthlytics
Elena.Park@healthlytics.com

Attachment: benchmark-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet with test cases)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap-up: procurement delay and request for short-term top-up

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for sending the test plan.

We can absolutely help keep the pilot alive while procurement finishes their review. I can provision a provisional 2-week access extension and a one-time top-up of $800 worth of credits (applies to hosted inference usage) immediately. If you expect to need more than that before the PO clears we'll need a quick approval from my manager (copied) to go beyond the standard allowance.

Next steps I suggest:
- I apply a 2-week extension today so the team can finish the benchmarks.
- Provision the $800 provisional credit now; we'll flag it on the account and reconcile once the PO arrives.
- Marcus, can you confirm the recommended settings so Elena's team uses credits efficiently (model variant, batching, and prefix cache suggestions)?
- Elena, if procurement can push a PO or signed SOW by Mar 4 we'll consider any additional temporary credits for the final week.

I attached a short interim-credit-agreement.pdf we use for these cases — it just formalizes the provisional top-up and the expectation of a PO/SOW. Please let me know if that works and I'll move ahead.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: interim-credit-agreement.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@healthlytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap-up: procurement delay and request for short-term top-up

Hey Elena — quick tech note on using the provisional credit efficiently:

- Use the quantized 8-bit variant we included in the catalog for latency-sensitive tests (same quality for your checkpoints, much lower cost).
- Set max_tokens to the actual expected response length and enable request-level caching for repeated prompts (we can whitelist the benchmark prompts).
- If the team will do concurrent runs, set batch_size to 4–8 depending on sequence length; that yields better throughput for GPU-backed pools.

I attached the se-test-config.txt with an example curl + SDK snippet and recommended flags. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to walk through if helpful.
